leads.summary: Related open China-region PR replaces Japanese input and reverses the selected language
leads.consequence: If #9695 also merges, `omarchy region china` after Japanese setup, with fcitx5 stopped (for example outside a graphical session), overwrites the whole profile without a backup, removing Mozc and restoring Ctrl+Space as a toggle even on JIS terminals. With fcitx5 running, its shutdown may instead restore its old profile over the region command's write, so that path needs a daemon test. In reverse order Japanese setup stops fcitx5, backs up but replaces Rime and, if the user accepts the locale prompt, sets Japanese LANG while the region still says China. Neither command reconciles the other's persisted configuration.

leads.summary: Related open Hangul setup loses Korean engine or default Korean activation keys on JIS installs
leads.consequence: If #11719 merges and a user installs Hangul first, running Japanese setup rewrites the profile without Hangul. In the reverse order, the Hangul command preserves Mozc and appends Hangul, but the Japanese command's replacement of TriggerKeys/ActivateKeys/DeactivateKeys has removed fcitx5's Hangul, Hangul_Hanja, and Hangul_Romaja default keys. leads.summary: Absent localectl layout silently selects US while the desktop remains JIS
leads.consequence: On a machine with XKBLAYOUT=jp in /etc/vconsole.conf but no parseable X11 Layout from `localectl status` (status error, or omitted layout), the script silently takes `us`: it writes keyboard-us, retains fcitx's Ctrl+Space toggle, skips the Henkan/Muhenkan hotkeys, and prints US instructions, while Hyprland installs JIS Ctrl+Space/zoom binds. The production code has no fallback to the vconsole value or mismatch warning; test fixtures always supply a valid localectl layout.
leads.triage: compared with Opus F1; corroborates F1 root cause (script reads localectl, Hyprland reads vconsole); covered by F1 suggested change; factual

leads.summary: A profile group named mozc without a Mozc item triggers a false already-installed result
leads.consequence: A valid fcitx5 group can be named `mozc`, even when its only item is `keyboard-us`. An exact line `Name=mozc` anywhere in the profile makes this setup return before adding the Mozc input-method item. It still prints that Mozc is installed and eventually says Japanese input is ready. Check only item names in the selected group, not all Name lines.
leads.triage: confirmed line 106 greps whole profile; dropped: requires a user-named group 'mozc' with no Mozc item; edge case not worth public space; factual

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** at `2d81b16`, the JIS gating, the keys both Hyprland binds send, and most of `omarchy setup japanese` behave as described in isolated tests and against upstream source. One input-parsing issue can leave some machines with Mozc as the only input method. The other notes concern existing profiles, the `Ctrl + Space` bind on JIS installs that keep the fcitx5 default toggle, and documentation wording.

**Verified** (sandboxed runs and source reading):
- `keyboard.jis()` loads both binds for `jp`, `"jp"` and `jp,us` (the last through the PR's own test), and none for `us` or `us,jp`. `input.lua` behaves as before (all existing layout assertions pass).
- Zoom bind: Chromium, foot and windows without a class get `Ctrl + KP_Add`; `obsidian` and `md.obsidian.Obsidian` get `Ctrl + ^`. The terminal-prefix bind runs `fcitx5-remote -c` only in windows tagged `terminal`, and it is non-consuming, so Hyprland still passes the key on (fcitx5 sees it first, see the `Ctrl + Space` section below). Hyprland 0.56.2 supports every API these binds use.
- `Henkan`, `Muhenkan` and `Zenkaku_Hankaku` are valid fcitx5 key names, and the profile sections match fcitx5's format. Stopping the unit before the edit is sound, because fcitx5 saves its profile on exit.
- On a realistic fcitx5 `config`, the JIS run replaces only the three hotkey lists, and a second run leaves the file byte-identical. `localectl set-locale` keeps existing `LC_*` overrides. `omarchy-display-text-size` still reads the size from the new font name.
- The PR's tests pass at the head. The full `test/shell.d` suite has the same 11 failing files on the head and the merge-base, so none come from this PR, and the new test file passes.

### `X11 Layout: (unset)` produces a `keyboard-(unset)` input method

[`x11_setting`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/2d81b16204f4f45788fbff71e9d9b4dfb0ae2c80/bin/omarchy-setup-japanese#L12-L14) falls back to `us` only when the value is empty ([line 93](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/2d81b16204f4f45788fbff71e9d9b4dfb0ae2c80/bin/omarchy-setup-japanese#L93)). When localed has no X11 layout, systemd's `localectl status` does not print an empty value. It prints `(unset)`: `localectl.c` sets the table's ersatz string to `TABLE_ERSATZ_UNSET`, and `bus-map-properties.c` maps an empty string to NULL.

```text
localectl status (stub, systemd's format):   X11 Layout: (unset)
  -> layout="(unset)"                        (not empty, so no fallback to us)
  -> profile: Default Layout=(unset)
              Name=keyboard-(unset)
  -> output:  "Added Mozc after keyboard-(unset) in your input methods."
control (X11 Layout: us)                  -> Name=keyboard-us
```

In a sandbox run, a `localectl` stub printed systemd's `(unset)` line and the script produced the lines above. The fcitx5 behaviour below comes from source and was not run: on load, fcitx5 removes an item with no registered input method (`inputmethodmanager.cpp`, "is not valid. Removed."), so the group keeps only Mozc.

**Impact:** on machines where localed has no X11 layout, the group has no keyboard-layout entry to switch back to, so fcitx5's toggle hotkeys have nothing to switch to. Omarchy's own code treats a missing `XKBLAYOUT` as a real state (`input.lua` falls back to `us`, and a migration notes that `vconsole.conf` only guarantees `KEYMAP`). Fresh installs through `systemd-firstboot --keymap` write `XKBLAYOUT` when systemd can map the keymap to an X11 layout (it maps `us` and `jp106`), so this mostly affects older or hand-configured installs.

**Suggested change:** read `XKBLAYOUT`/`XKBVARIANT` from `/etc/vconsole.conf`, as `default/hypr/keyboard.lua` does. That also keeps the script and the Hyprland binds on one source; today they can disagree when only `xorg.conf.d` sets a layout. The smaller fix is to treat `(unset)` as empty. A stub case that prints `(unset)` would cover it.

### An existing profile without Mozc is replaced, not extended

When `~/.config/fcitx5/profile` has no Mozc, the script backs it up and writes a new one-group profile. In a sandbox run, a profile with `keyboard-us` and `pinyin` ended up with `keyboard-us` and `mozc`, plus `profile.bak.<epoch>` next to it. The script only prints `Added Mozc after keyboard-us in your input methods.`, and the manual says the command "adds Mozc after your keyboard layout". The PR description is accurate ("backed up first"), but the text users see is not.

**Impact:** users who already type Chinese, Korean or another language through fcitx5 lose that input method and are not told a backup exists. For a profile fcitx5 generated with a single keyboard, nothing is lost.

**Suggested change:** append Mozc to the existing group when it is missing, or print that the previous input methods were replaced and where the backup is, and say so in the manual.

### On JIS, the terminal `Ctrl + Space` bind competes with the fcitx5 default toggle

The [prefix bind](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/2d81b16204f4f45788fbff71e9d9b4dfb0ae2c80/default/hypr/bindings/jis.lua#L45-L49) is active on every JIS install, whether or not `omarchy setup japanese` has run. fcitx5's default `TriggerKeys` include `Control+space`, and the manual's existing paragraph tells users to add an engine with `fcitx5-configtool`, which keeps that default unless they pick another key. From source, not a live session:

```text
Ctrl + Space in a terminal (JIS, default fcitx5 hotkeys, Mozc added)
  Hyprland: bind matches -> spawns `fcitx5-remote -c` (async) -> key passed on
  fcitx5:   Control+space is a trigger key -> toggles the input method
  also:     Deactivate runs on the same input context
  result:   one toggle direction is undone in terminals (the order was not timed)
```

**Impact:** for JIS users who added Mozc (or another input method) themselves or through another route and kept `Ctrl + Space` as the toggle, it stops toggling reliably in terminals. Zenkaku/Hankaku still works, and other windows are unaffected. Users who run the new command are not affected, because it removes `Ctrl + Space` from the toggle.

**Suggested change:** state in the manual that on JIS the terminal-prefix behaviour assumes `Ctrl + Space` is not the fcitx5 toggle (run `omarchy setup japanese`, or remove it in `fcitx5-configtool`). Alternatively, skip `fcitx5-remote -c` while `Control+space` is still a trigger key.

**Documentation notes:**
- `resetStateWhenFocusIn` defaults to `No` in every sampled fcitx5 release that has the option (5.1.9 through 5.1.23; the sampled releases up to 5.1.7 don't have it), and only `All` and `Program` reset state on focus. The comment at [line 180](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/2d81b16204f4f45788fbff71e9d9b4dfb0ae2c80/bin/omarchy-setup-japanese#L180-L183) ("The default resets every window") and the manual's "keeps Japanese input on when you switch between windows" therefore don't describe a change for default configs. If input was seen dropping on window switches with a default config, the cause is elsewhere.
- The manual's JIS table lists Henkan and Muhenkan as defaults that apply to JIS installs, but they only take effect after the command runs. The zoom and terminal-prefix rows are automatic, and Zenkaku/Hankaku already toggles through fcitx5's default hotkeys.
- The `jis.lua` comment says "the terminals all" zoom on `Ctrl + KP_Add`. kitty's default zoom key is `ctrl+shift+kp_add`. kitty also did not zoom on JIS `Ctrl + Shift + ;` before this PR, so this is wording, not a regression.
- On JIS the three hotkey lists are replaced entirely, so any other toggle keys (for example fcitx5's default `Hangul`) are removed along with `Ctrl + Space`.

**Optional test improvement:** no test calls the `jis.lua` callbacks. Diagnostic mutants that drop `non_consuming` (which would swallow the prefix), run `fcitx5-remote -c` in every window, send `KP_Subtract` instead of `KP_Add`, or delete the Obsidian override all pass both Lua tests. A test that runs the two callbacks with a fake `hl` would catch them. Likewise, "fcitx5 is down while its profile is rewritten" only compares the order of the stop and start calls, and a mutant that stops fcitx5 after writing the profile still passes. Having the `systemctl` stub snapshot the profile at stop and at start would pin the ordering.

**Related open PRs:** #9634 adds a separate one-step Mozc setup (`omarchy-setup-input-mozc`) with its own menu entry and rewrites the same fcitx5 paragraph in the manual. #11719 (Hangul) and #12312 (Traditional Chinese) use the `omarchy-setup-input-<engine>` naming; all three put their entries under a `Setup > Input Method` submenu, while this PR adds `Japanese` directly under Setup. #12920 also writes `~/.config/fcitx5/profile`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head against its merge-base, plus upstream Hyprland 0.56.2, fcitx5 (5.1.23 and sampled older releases), systemd v261, Mozc and kitty source. The PR's tests, the full `test/shell.d` suite, a callback harness for `jis.lua`, setup-script scenarios with every system command stubbed, and diagnostic mutants ran in an isolated sandbox. No live Hyprland, fcitx5 or Mozc session and no real key events were used, so key-delivery order and timing come from source. `test/cli` stops early in the sandbox (same on both sides), so the new command's CLI metadata was checked by reading it.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
